indicators.flag: A large volume of cash is delivered to a U.S.-based financial institution via an ACS on behalf of a customer who operates a Mexico-based business, a business located near the U.S. southwest border, or a U.S.-based company with an affiliated Mexico-based business. Following the delivery, the customer then rapidly moves the funds to a financial institution based in Mexico, makes transfers to another business in the United States they own and operate, or purchases a large volume of goods.
indicators.red_flag: Armored-cash deposit by border/Mexico-linked customer then rapid funnel-out to Mexico FI or own US business (cash placement → cross-border pass-through)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.flag: Large volumes of cash are transported by an ACS or passenger vehicles to an U.S.-based MSB located along the southwest border and rapidly transferred to Mexico.
indicators.red_flag: Bulk cash into southwest-border MSB → rapid cross-border transfer to Mexico (border-corridor pass-through)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: A customer that owns a Mexico-based business, or a customer with an affiliated Mexico-based business, receives a large credit from a U.S.-based ACS into their account at a U.S.-based financial institution.
indicators.red_flag: Large armored-car-service credit to Mexico-linked-business account (third-party cash channel funding)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C16 (Third-party / nominee funding & legal-professional channel detection); data D2.

indicators.flag: A customer that owns a Mexico-based business receives a large credit into their account at a U.S.-based financial institution after depositing bulk cash into the U.S.-based financial institution’s vault at a U.S.-based ACS secure storage facility.
indicators.red_flag: Bulk-cash vault deposit via ACS storage facility → large account credit (cash placement at armored-cash channel)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C5 (Cash-intensity / cash-placement anomaly detection); data D2.

indicators.flag: A customer that owns a Mexico-based business receives a large cross-border wire transfer to their account at a U.S.-based financial institution from a Canada-based financial institution.
indicators.red_flag: Large inbound cross-border wire from Canada FI to Mexico-linked-business account (high-risk-corridor inflow)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.section: Red Flags for Armored Car Services
indicators.flag: A business in Mexico, near the southwest border of the United States, organizes the transportation of a large volume of cash to multiple locations throughout the United States by an ACS or air transport, for no business or apparent lawful purpose, before it is finally delivered to a U.S.-based financial institution or a Federal Reserve Bank location.
indicators.red_flag: Border-business-organized multi-location bulk-cash movement with no lawful purpose before FI delivery (fan-out cash transport)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C3 (Multi-originator funnel-in / fan-out network detection).

indicators.section: Red Flags for Armored Car Services
indicators.flag: A Mexico-based business transporting cash into the United States is reluctant to provide information, or provides inconsistent information, on who is the currency originator or where the funds are destined in Part II of a FinCEN Form 105 (CMIR).
indicators.red_flag: Reluctant / inconsistent CMIR (Form 105) originator-or-destination disclosure on inbound cash (customer-cooperation gap)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Red Flags for Armored Car Services
indicators.flag: A non-bank Mexico-based business organizes the transport of large volumes of USD into the United States, that are not commensurate with the size of the business or the business profile.
indicators.red_flag: Inbound USD bulk-cash volume not commensurate with business size/profile (revenue-vs-operations anomaly)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a business account whose transaction inflows are disproportionate to its declared revenue, headcount, payroll, or operating-expense footprint relative to industry peers, escalating when revenue appears decoupled from any observable operational activity.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared profile and peer cohort
build_logic.source: business deposit ledger joined to KYC business profile + industry peer benchmarks
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.section: Red Flags for Armored Car Services
indicators.flag: A shipment of bulk cash is delivered via a Mexico or Canada-based ACS to a U.S.-based ACS without accompanying instructions or explanation for the purpose of the transaction.  The U.S.-based ACS then receives a request to transport the funds to a financial institution.
indicators.red_flag: Cross-border ACS-to-ACS bulk-cash handoff with no purpose/instructions before onward FI transport (layered cash channel)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C16 (Third-party / nominee funding & legal-professional channel detection); data D2.

indicators.section: Red Flags for Armored Car Services
indicators.flag: A Mexico-based business or individual requests that bulk cash be transported or accepted by a U.S. financial institution but does not provide a clear explanation of the source of the funds.
indicators.red_flag: Bulk-cash transport/acceptance request with no clear source-of-funds explanation (source-of-funds gap)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.
